disagreements.topic: Value of the SpaceX stake after the post-IPO decline
disagreements.positions: Agents 2, 3 and 5 still use the $94B SpaceX mark from Q2. Agent 4 marks it down to about $66B, assuming SPCX was about $213 at the end of Q2 and is now $148.68.
disagreements.resolution: Both are off. Alphabet holds about 551M SPCX shares, and the $94.1B Q2 mark implies about $170.86 a share at June 30, not $213. At $148.68 on 9/25 the stake is worth about $82B. The drop is about $12B pre-tax, or roughly $0.75 a share after tax, not the ~$2 a share agent 4 assumed. The $94B users are about $1 a share too high and agent 4 is about $1 a share too low, so the errors roughly cancel in the mean. $14.1B stays locked until Q3 2027. There will be a GAAP mark-to-market loss in Q3, but it is excluded from core EPS.
disagreements.evidence: Motley Fool 2026-07-23/07-28 (551M shares, about 4.9% ownership, $170.86 quarter-end price); Q2 2026 10-Q ($80.0B short-term restricted plus $14.1B long-term restricted through Q3 2027); SPCX close $148.68 (market cap about $2.02T).

disagreements.topic: Dilution from the June 2026 equity program
disagreements.positions: Agent 4 alone trims NTM EPS by about 1% for a $40B ATM and $19B of 6.25% mandatory convertible preferred. Agents 1 and 5 apply a generic 1.5-3% haircut to consensus. Agents 2 and 3 fold dilution into FY2028 growth of +13-18%.
disagreements.resolution: The instruments are real. The total raise was $84.75B: $15B of common and $15B of mandatory convertible preferred underwritten (10-Q: about $18.0B of 6.25% Series A/B MCPS outstanding), plus a $40B ATM starting Q3. The ATM is mainly a sell-to-cover mechanism for employee RSU tax withholding. It replaces net-share settlement, so it adds only about 0.2-0.3% a year of share count, not $40B of new float. The MCPS dividend (about $1.1B a year) and eventual conversion (about 3 years out, after the horizon) are worth about 0.5-1% of EPS. The haircuts of about 1-3% that agents already apply cover this, so it does not move the mean.

disagreements.topic: Fair-value method mix (whether a DCF is included)
disagreements.positions: Fair values range from $360 to $375 (mean about $367). Agents 2, 4 and 5 give 20-25% weight to a DCF at $313-318, while agents 1 and 3 lean on P/E and SOTP at $365-377. All P/E methods converge on about 22x NTM core EPS of about $16.2-16.9 plus $12-19 a share of stakes, giving about $367-377.
disagreements.resolution: This is a methodology choice, not a factual dispute. The DCF discount reflects 2027 capex of about $257B, which is consensus and already priced in the 22x multiple. The spread is less than 5% of price and all five ladders put the median near $362-370. Nothing to settle with search.
disagreements.evidence: Agents' fair_value.methods; FactSet 2027 capex consensus of about $257B cited by all five.

disagreements.positions: Stake credit ranges from about $12/sh (agent 3) to about $19/sh (agent 2). The IPO uplift is taken as $3-8.5/sh, probability-weighted at 50-65%.
disagreements.resolution: As of 9/27 there is still no public S-1. There was a confidential draft on June 1, and the WSJ reports a November listing at about $2T. Ownership is undisclosed; analysts estimate 10-15%, and it was about 14% before later rounds. At $2T and 10-15%, the pre-tax uplift over the $124.3B carrying value is about $76-176B, or about $5-11/sh after 21% tax. The agents' $3-8.5/sh expected values sit inside that range. The spread among them is worth about $5/sh, and the IPO is a right-tail catalyst rather than a shift in the center.
disagreements.evidence: Motley Fool 2026-09-14 and 2026-09-24; NeoTeo on the confidential S-1.

disagreements.topic: Tail thickness and the right tail
disagreements.positions: Agent 4 has the fattest right tail: P(>=688) 0.037 and P(>=860) 0.010, against 0.021-0.024 and 0.004-0.005 for the other four. P(>=344) ranges from 0.563 to 0.585.
disagreements.resolution: Nothing found supports an outsized right tail. Twice spot ($688) would need about 30x NTM EPS of about $17 plus stakes, above any multiple GOOGL has held in a decade apart from brief peaks. The other four agents' ~0.023 fits sigma of about 0.32 with a modest fat-tail component. I trim the far right tail slightly and leave the center unchanged.
disagreements.evidence: Realized vol of about 31% cited by all agents; multiple history in the agents' P/E methods; analyst average target of about $422-436 (well below $688).

disagreements.topic: Q3 2026 earnings date and thesis-break level
disagreements.positions: Agents 4 and 5 give Q3 earnings as 10-27, agent 2 as 10-28, and agents 1 and 3 as unconfirmed. The thesis break is $245 (agents 1 and 4 in round 1; agent 4 now), $250 (agent 1) or $255 (agents 2, 3 and 5).
disagreements.resolution: Alphabet has not yet announced the Q3 call date; its IR lists only the Q1 and Q2 date announcements. Late October is likely, but the exact date is unknown and does not matter for a 12-month close. On the thesis break, all agents agree it means about 16-17x FY2027 core EPS of about $14.9 with no stake credit, which requires an actual EPS downgrade. The $245-255 spread is noise, so I keep $250, about the mean of the agents' $251.
disagreements.evidence: abc.xyz investor news (no Q3 date release as of 9/27); Q2 call closing remarks.

fair_value.method: Reconciled from the five revised fair values ($360-375, mean $366.6). The P/E methods converge on about 22x NTM core EPS of about $16.2-16.9 at the horizon ($356-372) plus stakes. Stakes are worth about $13-15/sh after correcting SpaceX to about $82B (551M shares x $148.68) and crediting Anthropic at its $124.3B carrying value after tax, plus about $4-5/sh of probability-weighted uplift from the November IPO. The DCF cross-checks ($313-340) are weighted about 20% and reflect the ~$257B 2027 capex consensus. The corrections cancel, so fair value stays at the mean, about $367 (+7% vs $343.92).

changes.why: Agent 4's right tail (0.075/0.037/0.010) is an outlier with no supporting evidence. Twice spot needs ~30x NTM EPS. Trimmed slightly toward the other four agents.
Rounding plus a slight smoothing so the upper tail stays monotone and consistent with the trimmed far tail. Economically immaterial.

changes.to: mean rounded to 3 dp (no substantive change)
changes.why: The only factual errors found (SpaceX mark: agent 4 too low, others too high by about $1/sh; ATM dilution overstated by agent 4) are under $1/sh net and cancel across agents.
551M shares x $148.68. Agent 4's assumed Q2-end price of $213 was wrong; it was $170.86.
About 17x consensus FY2027 core EPS with no stake credit. All agents frame it as an earnings downgrade, and the $10 spread is noise.

confidence_reason: The revised forecasts are very tightly clustered: P(>=344) is 0.563-0.585, fair values are $360-375 and thesis breaks are $245-255. My checks found only small errors: SpaceX was misvalued in both directions by about $1/sh, and agent 4 overstated the ATM's dilution. These cancel across agents. The remaining differences are methodology choices (DCF weight) that search cannot settle. My only change is a slight trim of the far right tail, and it may not be in the right direction, so the mean should stand.
thesis_break_reason: At about $250 (-27%) GOOGL would trade near 17x consensus FY2027 core EPS of about $14.9 with no credit for the ~$13-15/sh of SpaceX/Anthropic stakes, about 6% above the $235.84 52-week low. With core operating income growing about 30% and FY2027 revisions running 8 up to 1 down, reaching that level would signal an actual earnings downgrade (the 2022 pattern, the one failed rebound in 10 prior 15% pullbacks), not multiple noise. The main causes would be agentic assistants (Meta Muse, ChatGPT) pushing Search growth to single digits, Cloud's $514B backlog failing to convert, or a February 2027 capex guide far above about $257B with FCF negative into 2028 and more dilution.
key_drivers: Core EPS path: FY2027 consensus of about $14.92 core (+25%), revisions 8 up to 1 down; NTM core EPS at the horizon of about $16.2-16.9 at about 22x gives $356-372 before stakes

2027 capex (FactSet consensus about $257B, formal guide in early February 2027) against FCF: Q2 FCF was -$5.9B, YTD about +$4B, buybacks halted, $84.75B equity program including about $18B of 6.25% mandatory convertible preferred
Search resilience against agentic assistants (Meta Muse, ChatGPT) versus Cloud at +82% with a $514B backlog and TPU system sales in 2027

Equity stakes: SpaceX about $82B at $148.68 (551M shares; $14.1B locked until Q3 2027) and Anthropic carried at $124.3B. A reported November 2026 IPO at about $2T would add roughly $5-11/sh after tax depending on the undisclosed 10-15% ownership
Base rate: 9 of 10 prior 15% drawdowns were higher a year later, and the exception required EPS -19%, so there is a mild upward tilt but the left tail is still set by an earnings downgrade
summary: The five revised forecasts agree closely: median about $365, P(>=spot) about 0.57, fair value about $367 (+7%). Round-2 checks found only small, offsetting factual errors. The SpaceX stake is about $82B (551M shares at $148.68), not $94B or $66B. The June equity program's $40B ATM is mainly a sell-to-cover mechanism for employee tax withholding, not large new dilution. I keep the forecasters' mean ladder and trim only the far right tail slightly, with low confidence. The swing factors are the February 2027 capex guide, Search holding up against agentic assistants, and the reported November Anthropic IPO. A close below about $250 would signal an earnings-downgrade thesis break.
